query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) in eutectic high-entropy alloys can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility by facilitating dislocation transmission and relieving stress concentrations.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase lamellar structure
generation.intervention: Introduction of stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) through a tailored thermo-mechanical process
generation.conditions: Room temperature and uniaxial tensile loading
generation.mechanism: The coherent interfaces of the SCCPs facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, while the δ-lamellae hinder dislocation motion and the γ″ particles provide order hardening and lattice misfit strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and room-temperature tensile ductility compared to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.baseline: Unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase lamellar structure
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the SCCPs depends on the specific composition and processing conditions of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of SCCP formation and its influence on dislocation mobility and stress concentrations is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature on eutectic high-entropy alloys with and without SCCPs
measurements: Microstructural characterization via EBSD, TEM, STEM, and APT
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of SCCPs does not result in improved strength and room-temperature tensile ductility, the hypothesis is falsified

System: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (at.%) refractory high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase bcc/fcc structure. Processing: Arc melting followed by homogenization at 1200 °C for 5 h, hot rolling at 1200 °C (80% reduction), cold rolling at 25 °C (75% reduction), annealing at 900 °C for 5 min, and aging at 650 °C for 20 h followed by water quenching. Test conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature (strain rate 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹) and elevated temperatures up to 800 °C (strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); microstructural characterization via EBSD, TEM, STEM, and APT. System: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA).
